description: Reference tuning and its drift (a histogram of spectral peaks' distance from the tempered grid, with mains hum left out), pitch-class profiles of the treble and the bass referenced to that tuning, the key as a note collection (its likeliest tonic and mode a guess, never named), and sensory dissonance, by Essentia and NumPy. Decodes twice more and repeats frames' spectral peak picking, which the bank does not hold: about 1.5 times frames' time (ADR 0074). Version 3 replaced TuningFrequency, added the profiles, mode, and key regions, and moved chords to the chords extractor; version 4 leaves mains hum out of the pitch gate, the tuning, and the profiles, names a tonic only where it leads by a margin, lays the key regions out by note collection, and counts the tuning's windows; version 5 reports a recording's tuning only from enough of its windows, and chooses the tonic among the collection's notes by their share of the bass, favouring its major or minor tonic, with a calibrated confidence; version 6 names no tonic: every span is labelled and valued by its note collection, and tonic_named is false everywhere.

pitched.description: 1 where the frame sounds and its five-second block's loud peaks below 2 kHz, mains hum left out, agree on a tuning; 0 for silence, talk, noise, and hum

tuning_frequency.description: the frequency of A4 the recording is tuned to: the confidence-weighted median of the confident windows; 440.0 with confidence 0 when no window is confident or too few are (fewer than four, unless the recording has fewer windows than that and all are, or fewer than half of the windows at least half pitched)

tuning_cents.description: the tuning's distance from 440 Hz, in [-50, 50)

tuning_confidence.description: share of the sounding frames' loud peak magnitude below 2 kHz within 15 cents of the tuning; 0 when the tuning is not reported (too few confident windows), about 0.31 for noise

tuning_window_count.description: how many windows are at least half pitched and at least 0.4 confident, which tuning_cents is taken from when there are enough of them (at least four, or every window of a shorter recording, and at least half of the windows at least half pitched); 0 when none is

tuning_windows.description: every window of about 20 s every 10 s, centred midway between its first and last frame's centres (the last may be shorter): its tuning in cents near the confident windows' median (tuning_cents when that is reported) (0 when it has no pitched frame), the concentration of its sounding frames' peaks about that tuning (its confidence), and its share of pitched frames; a window at least half pitched and at least 0.4 confident counts towards tuning_cents

tuning_drift.description: the tuning windows that are at least half pitched; value: the window's tuning in cents from 440 Hz, near the confident windows' median (tuning_cents when that is reported)

drift_spread_cents.description: tenth to ninetieth percentile of tuning_drift's values; 0 for fewer than two windows

detuned.description: true when tuning_cents is more than 40 cents from 440 Hz, where a profile referenced to 440 Hz (frames/hpcp) splits each pitch class over two bins; chroma, bass_chroma, and the key are referenced to the measured tuning and are not affected

detuned_spans.description: the tuning_drift windows more than 40 cents from 440 Hz; value: the window's tuning in cents

key.description: tonic of the pitched frames' note collection, as Essentia names notes (A, Bb, B, C, C#, D, Eb, E, F, F#, G, Ab): the collection's note with the most bass, favouring its major or minor tonic; a best guess when tonic_named is false; empty when no frame is pitched

scale.description: major for an ionian, lydian, or mixolydian mode, minor for any other; empty when no frame is pitched

mode.description: ionian, dorian, phrygian, lydian, mixolydian, aeolian, locrian, harmonic minor, or melodic minor; empty when no frame is pitched

scale_notes.description: the mode's seven notes from the tonic up, separated by spaces (F dorian: F G Ab Bb C D Eb); empty when no frame is pitched

key_strength.description: correlation of the profile with the named mode's template, -1 to 1; 0 when no frame is pitched

collection.description: the note collection whose best mode's template correlates best with the profile, named by its ionian tonic for the diatonic modes (Eb major scale, for F dorian) or by its own (C harmonic minor scale, C melodic minor scale); empty when no frame is pitched

collection_margin.description: how far the collection's best correlation leads the best reading on other notes; 0 when no frame is pitched

tonic_margin.description: how far the tonic's evidence (its bass share, a quarter of its treble share, and 0.08 more for the collection's major or minor tonic) leads the collection's next note; 0 when no frame is pitched

tonic_confidence.description: the chance that the tonic is right, given the collection: the softmax of the collection's seven notes' evidence at temperature 0.07, read at the tonic; 1/7 when nothing tells them apart, beyond the favour; on one album its mean matched the share of published key claims the tonic agreed with (0.43 against 0.45), but it did not tell the tracks it got right from those it did not; 0 when no frame is pitched

tonic_named.description: false everywhere since version 6 (version 5: true when tonic_confidence was at least 0.5): key, mode, and scale are the best guess among the collection's modes, and only collection and scale_notes' notes are to be read

keys.description: windows of about 30 s every 15 s that are at least half pitched; label: the note collection (Eb major scale); value: its collection_margin

key_regions.description: the timeline of note collections: the keys windows' collections on a path that pays 0.1 for each change, laid end to end (each keeping the stretch nearer its centre than its neighbours'), runs of one collection merged; label: the collection; value: how far the collection's best correlation over the region's own frames leads the best reading on other notes (negative where another collection fits them better)

chroma.description: pitch-class profile of the peaks from 100 to 5,000 Hz, bin 0 is A, referenced to the frame's tuning (the confident windows' tunings interpolated); not normalised; 0 below the level gate

bass_chroma.description: the same from the peaks from 40 to 250 Hz

dissonance.description: sensory dissonance of each frame's peaks within 40 dB of its loudest, 0 to 0.5; 0 for a frame below the -60 dBFS gate or with no peaks; talk and noise above the gate have a value, so mask with pitched for music
